title: Chrysler (FCA US, LLC): FUEL:THROTTLE LINKAGES AND CONTROL:PEDAL (2,218 affected)
Yokohama Tire Corporation: TIRES:PLY (572 affected)
summary: TIRES DO NOT CONFORM TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD NO. 109, NEW PNEUMATIC TIRES. A BULGE MAY DEVELOP IN THE SIDE WALL AREA, OR NOISE AND VIBRATION MAY BE DETECTED WHEN DRIVING.

title: Nissan North America, Inc.: STRUCTURE:HOOD ASSEMBLY:LATCHES (86,000 affected)
summary: DUE TO IMPROPER OPERATION OF THE SECONDARY HOOD LATCH BY OWNERS USING EXCESSIVE FORCE ON THE LEVER, THE HOOD LATCH ASSEMBLY MAY BECOME DAMAGED, RESULTING IN SEPARATION OF THE SECONDARY LATCH FROM THE LATCH ASSEMBLY.

title: Mack Trucks, Inc.: STRUCTURE:FIFTH WHEEL ASSEMBLY (64 affected)
summary: DUE TO IMPROPER AND INADEQUATE WELDING PRACTICES, THE FIFTH WHEEL ON THE INVOLVED VEHICLES IS DEFECTIVE. FRAME MOUNTED SUPPORTS MAY HAVE INCOMPLETE OR POOR QUALITY WELDS. THE WELDS COULD SUBSEQUENTLY FAIL ALLOWING SEPARATION OF THE TRACTOR FROM THE TRAILER.

title: Mack Trucks, Inc.: STRUCTURE:DOOR ASSEMBLY:LATCHES AND LOCKS (1,300 affected)
summary: THE DOOR LATCHES MAY BE DEFECTIVE BECAUSE A PAWL SPRING WAS NOT MANUFACTURED TO SPECIFICATIONS. THE PAWL SPRING DOES NOT CREATE PROPER TENSION ON THE PAWL, (A PART OF THE DOOR LATCH MECHANISM). THIS CONSTITUTES A NON-COMPLIANCE WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD NO. 206, "DOOR LATCHES AND DOOR RETENTION COMPONENTS".

title: Mack Trucks, Inc.: SUSPENSION:I-BEAM:SOLID:FRONT LEAF SPRING ASSEMBLY (2,198 affected)
summary: THE SPRING CENTER BOLT IS NOT THE PROPER SIZE OR LENGTH. AS A RESULT, LOCATION AND ALIGNMENT OF THE SPRING TO THE FRONT AXLE MAY NOT BE CORRECT. IF THE FRONT SPRING CLIPS LOOSEN, THE INADEQUATE CENTER BOLT MAY RESULT IN SPRING TO AXLE MISALIGNMENT, SHIFTING OF THE AXLE, AND LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL.

title: MARMON MOTOR COMPANY: ENGINE:MOUNTS (97 affected)
summary: WELDS THAT ATTACH THE RADIATOR SUPPORT CAN CRACK. CRACKS MAY OCCUR IN THE RADIATOR SUPPORT AND THE ENGINE SUPPORT AT OR NEAR THE WELDS THAT JOIN THEM. IT IS ALSO POSSIBLE FOR THE ENGINE TO CAUSE THE ENGINE SUPPORT TO SAG.

title: ROSS GEAR DIV.: SUSPENSION:INDEPENDENT FRONT CONTROL ARM:LOWER:BAL (962 affected)
summary: POOR METALLIC COMPOUND USED TO CONSTRUCT BALL JOINTS. THESE BALL JOINTS MAY WEAR IN A SHORT TIME UNDER NORMAL OPERATION. WORN BALL JOINTS MAY CAUSE A SEPARATION OF PARTS IN THE BALL JOINT HOUSING.

title: Volkswagen Group of America, Inc.: BRAKES:HYDRAULIC:FITTINGS:NON-METALLIC (9,500 affected)
summary: THE CLIP LOCATED ABOVE THE EXHAUST PIPE WHERE IT ENTERS THE PRE-MUFFLER MAY MELT FROM EXCESSIVE HEAT CAUSED BY ENGINE IDLING.

title: RENAULT, INCORPORATED: INTERIOR SYSTEMS:ACTIVE RESTRAINTS:BELT BUCKLES (7,137 affected)
summary: THE FRONT SEAT BELT ASSEMBLY MAY REQUIRE MORE EFFORT THAN USUAL TO RELEASE AND FAILS TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD 209, "SEAT BELT ASSEMBLIES".

title: General Motors, LLC: VISUAL SYSTEMS:WINDSHIELD WIPER/WASHER SWITCH (973 affected)
summary: THE SWITCH USED MAY NOT BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE WIPER MOTOR. THIS SYSTEM, ALTHOUGH FUNCTIONAL, IS NOT IN COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD NO. 104, "WINDSHIELD WIPING AND WASHING SYSTEM". THE WINDSHIELD WIPER SPEED MAY REMAIN NEARLY CONSTANT WHETHER IN HIGH OR LOW SPEED MODE. THE STANDARD REQUIRES THAT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN HIGH AND LOW SPEED MUST BE AT LEAST 15 CYCLES PER MINUTE TO ACCOMODATE A VARIETY OF RAIN, SNOW, OR WHEEL SPRAY CONDITIONS.

title: DAYTON STEEL FOUNDRY CO.: TIRES (239 affected)
summary: A MAJORITY OF TIRES TESTED DID NOT MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD 109, NEW PNEUMATIC TIRES, HIGH SPEED TEST. TREAD SEPARATION OCCURRED ON THESE TIRES.

title: Chrysler (FCA US, LLC): FUEL:FUEL LINES:HOSES:NON-METALLIC (340,000 affected)
summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR FUEL LEAKAGE EXISTS IN THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT AT THE FUEL RESERVOIR SEAM AND ITS HOSE CONNECTIONS. THE FUEL RESERVOIR IS A SILVER COLORED CAN MOUNTED TO THE AIR CLEANER.

title: INTERNATIONAL TRUCK & ENGINE CORPORATION: POWER TRAIN:AXLE ASSEMBLY:HOUSING:AXLE SHAFT (2,350 affected)
summary: THE WELDING OF THE BRAKE MOUNTING FLANGES TO THE REAR AXLE MAY BE DEFECTIVE AND MAY BREAK. IF THIS WELD WERE TO SEPARATE DURING VEHICLE OPERATION, ADJACENT BRAKE LINES COULD BE DAMAGED.

title: General Motors, LLC: POWER TRAIN:AXLE ASSEMBLY:SHAFT AXLE (3,100,000 affected)
summary: REAR AXLE ASSEMBLY MAY HAVE AXLES THAT WERE IMPROPERLY MANUFACTURED. THIS CONDITION MAY RESULT IN SEPARATION OF THE AXLE SHAFT AND WHEEL ASSEMBLY FROM THE VEHICLE.

title: FIRESTONE STEEL PROD. CO.: WHEELS:DISC:SPIDER (5,690 affected)
summary: A SURFACE FLAW WHICH OCCURRED DURING MANUFACTURE OF THE WHEELS MAY LEAD TO A FOLD OR CRACK UNDER SEVERE LOADING OR EXTENDED USE.

title: Chrysler (FCA US, LLC): FUEL:FUEL LINES:METALLIC (82,500 affected)
summary: THE METAL FUEL SUPPLY TUBE MAY CRACK AT THE FUEL PUMP END DUE TO VIBRATION. THE CRACK MAY RESULT IN FUEL LEAKAGE. (THE FUEL SUPPLY TUBE CONNECTS THE FUEL PUMP TO THE FUEL FILTER.)

title: PEUGEOT, INC.: FUEL:FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY:CAP:FILLER (18,232 affected)
summary: THE FUEL CAPS ON THE INVOLVED VEHICLES DO NOT SEAL PROPERLY AND ARE NOT IN COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARD NO. 301, "FUEL SYSTEM INTEGRITY." CONTACT WITH FUEL CAUSES THE FUEL CAP GASKET TO SWELL, PREVENTING ADEQUATE SEALING BETWEEN CAP AND FILLER OPENING.

title: Volkswagen Group of America, Inc.: FUEL:FUEL INJECTION:UNKNOWN TYPE:LINE:HOSE (4,000 affected)
summary: THE HOSE CONNECTED TO THE PUMP LOCATED INSIDE THE FUEL TANK MAY BECOME DISCONNECTED WHEN THE VEHICLE IS IN USE. IF THIS HAPPENS, THE FUEL SUPPLY TO THE ENGINE WILL BE INTERRUPTED, CAUSING THE VEHICLE TO STALL.

title: General Motors, LLC: INTERIOR SYSTEMS:ACTIVE RESTRAINTS:BELT RETRACTORS (19 affected)
summary: THE VEHICLES WERE ASSEMBLED WITH FRONT SEAT BELT RETRACTORS WHICH MAY NOT PERFORM ADEQUATELY DURING A COLLISION.

title: General Motors, LLC: SUSPENSION:SINGLE AXLE:REAR:CONTROL ARM (9,290 affected)
summary: THE REAR AXLE CONTROL ARM LOCATES AND HELPS CONTROL AXLE MOVEMENT; IT ATTACHES TO THE FRAME WITH A BRACKET. THE REAR CONTROL ARM BRACKET ATTACHING BOLTS USED ON SOME OF THE INVOLVED VEHICLES MAY FRACTURE. FRACTURE OF ALL FOUR BOLTS ON ONE SIDE OF THE VEHICLE CAN RESULT IN THE CONTROL ARM DROPPING ENOUGH TO CUT THE REAR BRAKE HOSE. A SEVERED BRAKE HOSE WOULD RESULT IN BRAKE FLUID LOSS AND PARTIAL LOSS OF BRAKING ABILITY.
